results.question: What drove GOP vs budget in October for the group?
results.why: A bridge from budget GOP to actual GOP, line by line.

widgets.title: October 2026 group GOP beat budget by about €1.04M, driven by rooms

results.answer:
October 2026 group GOP came in at €15.41M against a budget of €14.37M, which is about €1.04M ahead. I read "October" as 2026 because the business date is 20 Nov 2026.

- **Rooms revenue:** +€1.04M over budget. This is the main driver.
- **F&B:** revenue was €0.97M under budget, but F&B expense was €0.78M under as well. The net hit to GOP is about €0.18M.
- **M&E and other revenue:** M&E was €0.20M under budget and other revenue €0.12M under. Nothing offset these.
- **Other costs:** rooms expense was €0.22M under budget, and A&G, S&M and maintenance together were about €0.36M under. Utilities were roughly on budget. Part of this cost saving may simply follow lower volumes.
- **Unallocated in budget:** −€0.08M. This is the part of budget GOP that its own revenue and expense lines don't explain.

The GOP beat rests on rooms, and the F&B and M&E shortfalls were largely covered by lower costs. Next move: pull the F&B and M&E lines by hotel (get_pnl, view lines) to find which properties missed on revenue. Then check whether their cost savings are structural or only a timing effect.

results.question: Show occupancy for the next 14 nights by hotel
results.why: Hotels × nights is a grid: 20 hotels over 14 nights.

widgets.title: Occupancy on the books, 20 Nov – 3 Dec, by hotel

results.answer:
The heatmap shows occupancy on the books for all 20 hotels from 20 Nov to 3 Dec. These are on-the-books figures, not actuals.

- **Strongest:** DXB1 is at 94–98% on 20–21 Nov. TYO, NYC, VIE and EZE also have peaks above 85–90% in the first few nights.
- **Weakest:** LON1 (50.8% on 20 Nov) and YYZ and LON2 (45–46% on 22 Nov). Several hotels, including BER, CHI, NYC and LIS, drop to about 52–54% on Sunday 22 Nov.

**Next move:** Check `get_rate_position` for the high-occupancy nights at DXB1, TYO and NYC, because they may be underpriced. Check pickup for LON1, LON2 and YYZ on the soft nights.

results.question: How is Amsterdam's mobile booking funnel doing?
results.why: Sessions, searches, checkout starts and bookings only shrink: a funnel.

widgets.title: Amsterdam mobile loses 57% of checkouts: 312 starts, 134 bookings
Mobile checkout completion fell from 100% to about 45% from the week of 19 Oct

results.answer:
Amsterdam's mobile funnel looks broken at checkout. Mobile checkout completion was 100% through the week of 12 Oct. Since the week of 19 Oct it has been about 40–55%. In the last 28 days, 312 mobile checkouts were started and only 134 completed (42.9%). Desktop is still at 100%, so the fault is specific to mobile.

- **Top of the funnel is healthy.** Mobile sessions and searches are in line with earlier weeks. The loss happens after the guest starts checkout.
- **Conversion has halved.** Mobile conversion fell from about 1.9% to 0.7–1.0%, against about 3% on desktop. Weekly mobile booking revenue fell from about €40–50k to about €15k.
- **Data feeds are fine.** All Amsterdam sources synced this morning, so this is not a stale feed.

**Next move:** Ask the web or IT team to test the mobile checkout on iOS and Android. Look first at payment or form steps that changed around 19 Oct. I can draft a workflow that flags this finding automatically if you want one.

results.question: Give me the headline KPIs for Asia this month
results.why: A few headline numbers with last year: KPI tiles. Asked in Quick mode, which owes a widget too.

widgets.title: Asia is at 76.4% occupancy and 294 EUR RevPAR for November, both ahead of last year

results.answer:
Asia for November 2026 is ahead of last year on every headline: occupancy 76.4% (73.9% LY), ADR €385 (€379 LY), RevPAR €294 (€280 LY), and room revenue €6.06M (€5.77M LY).

Figures cover 1–30 November, with actuals up to 19 November and the rest on the books. Rooms sold are 15,712 against 15,198 last year.

Next move: check whether the on-the-books nights in late November are pacing as strongly as the ADR gain suggests, using get_pace for the Asia hotels. I can run that next if you want it.
